title: Streaming lifecycle + plugin hooks: PRD (rough)
content:
Context and motivation:

Problem: our current hosted streaming surface focuses on incremental output and tool-handshake ergonomics for single-invocation flows, but we lack a first-class model for request lifecycle events, plugin lifecycle hooks, and explicit extension points for SDKs to manage progressive fidelity, prefetch, and interruption semantics. This gap causes ad-hoc implementations across client libraries and complicates integration with tool-chains (third-party connectors, database lookups, external tool runtimes) and observability.

Why this matters: teams building multi-stage flows (prefetch -> stream -> tool-call -> postprocess) need predictable lifecycle events (start, checkpoint, pre-tool, tool-result, finalize, abort) and a plugin model to attach policy, telemetry, caching, and authorization without modifying core runtime. This will reduce duplicate code in client SDKs, make fallbacks consistent, and unlock richer telemetry for quality regressions tied to specific lifecycle phases.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Define a streaming lifecycle model and canonical event set that supports incremental output and tool calls.
- Provide a plugin hook specification (server + SDK) that is lightweight, backward-compatible, and extensible by customers and Redwood plugins.
- Surface SDK ergonomics that make it trivial for clients to attach: (a) prefetch policies, (b) tool call adapters, (c) structured-output validators, (d) abort/retry strategies.
- Ensure telemetry captures lifecycle boundaries and plugin execution outcomes for alerting/evals.
- Ship a minimal beta API and Node + Python SDK primitives for internal partners in Q1 pilot.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does NOT propose a complete rework of streaming wire-protocol. Focus is on lifecycle semantics and extension points.
- Not addressing Dedicated private install footprint differences in depth (that will be follow-up).

Proposed lifecycle model (canonical event sequence):
- invocation.start: inbound call accepted, headers & route resolved; early auth checks.
- prefetch.hint: (optional) client-provided signals about likely tokens or external context; allows routing/prefetch policies.
- output.delta: incremental text/frame fragments as today. Each delta annotated with sequence id and checkpoint state.
- checkpoint.stable: optional snapshot point where server marks a durable partial result (used for resume/replay).
- pretool.invoke: server emits a structured intent for tool-calling; plugins can veto/modify.
- tool.invoke: tool bridge executes; bridging semantics include idempotency tokens and bounded timeout.
- tool.result: tool output frames; can be streamed or batched into a single result.
- postprocess.apply: optional server-side transformations (formatting, schema validation).
- invocation.finish: final output delivered; includes final metrics and model variant used.
- invocation.abort: terminal event for cancellations, quota kills, or fatal errors; contains abort reason and last checkpoint id.

Plugin hook model (principles):
- Hooks are lightweight callbacks that run at lifecycle boundaries. Plugins may be local (SDK-side), server-side (hosted runtime), or hybrid (coordination between server and SDK).
- Hooks must be deterministic and bounded in execution time; long-running work should be offloaded to async tasks referenced by id.
- Hooks must be able to: read/write request-scoped metadata, annotate telemetry, influence tool invocation payload, and request circuit-breakers (veto).
- Security: plugin code should never receive raw user data unless explicitly allowed by a policy flag. Plugins that need PII require opt-in and audit logging.

Canonical hooks (initial set):
- onStart(requestMeta) -> allow|deny|mutateMeta
- onPrefetch(hint) -> prefetchDecision (route|cancel|defer)
- onDelta(deltaFrame) -> annotate|drop|none (used by streaming validators)
- onCheckpoint(checkpointId) -> storeRef|noop
- onPretTool(intent) -> allow|veto|transformIntent
- onToolResult(toolMeta, toolPayload) -> enrichResponse|scrub|error
- onPostprocess(response) -> validate|rewrite|flag
- onFinish(summary) -> report|noop

SDK ergonomics (Node + Python primitives):
- Lightweight subscription API: request.lifecycle.subscribe(hookName, asyncHookFn) where asyncHookFn receives plain objects, returns a small action token (string) or throws to veto.
- Safe defaults: SDKs pre-register no-op hooks and a simple telemetry aggregator.
- Short-circuit helpers: request.lifecycle.once('pretool.invoke', (intent) => { if (intent.type === 'lookup') return { route: 'fast-path' } })
- Prefetch API: request.prefetch.hint({keys: [...], priority: 'low|med|high'}) -> returns prefetchHandle
- Resume API: client can request resume(token) and SDK will replay deltas until checkpoint match.

Wire & compatibility notes:
- Keep current chunked JSON streaming as-is; lifecycle additions are carried as top-level frames with an explicit lifecycle_type field (e.g. {lifecycle: "pretool.invoke", payload: {...}}). Existing clients will ignore unknown lifecycle frames.
- Introduce a small schema version in initial handshake: streamingProtocolVersion: 2. This enables staged rollout.

Observability & SLO implications:
- Instrumentation events per invocation: lifecycle.start_ts, pretool_latency_ms, tool_bridge_latency_ms, checkpoint_count, abort_reason, plugin_errors[].
- Telemetry tagging: attach customer token, model-version, route, plugin-ids invoked, and client-sdk-version. Keep PII out of top-level tags.
- New dashboards: lifecycle heatmap (phase durations), plugin error rate, tool-bridge tail latency.

Security & privacy:
- Plugins that request raw prompts must be documented and explicitly enabled per-organization. Audit log every plugin execution and include sampled payloads for debugging with redaction.
- Tool invocation payloads must be sanitized by default; SDKs will provide helpers to define scrubbing rules.

Rollout plan (high-level):
- Q4 internal design + API sketching; finalize canonical hooks.
- Q1: implement server-side lifecycle frames + pilot Node SDK hooks with 3 internal partners (console sync, developer-lab, search-agent).
- Q2: extend plugin registry, telemetry dashboards, and Python SDK. Begin external beta with 5 customers.
- Q3: iterate on plugin policy/permissions and expand client-language coverage.

Backward compat & migration: existing streaming clients will continue to work; to opt into lifecycle frames customers set streamingProtocolVersion: 2 in initial call. SDKs will default to v1 to avoid breaking behavior. Migration docs and a compatibility linter will be provided.

Open questions (priority ordered):
- What is the SLA/timeout we place on plugin hooks before auto-fallback? (30ms vs 200ms for pretool decisions)
- How do we expose plugin authoring for customers (sandboxed WASM vs server-managed JS)?
- Should plugins be able to modify tokens billed? (risk of cost leak)
- How to gate PII access across multi-tenant Hosted vs Dedicated?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Product + Infra sync (Laura, Riley, Samir) to agree on the 8 canonical hooks by 2024-10-10.
- Design doc for wire frames and handshake (owner: Diego) due 2024-10-20.
- Minimal Node SDK prototype demonstrating request.lifecycle.subscribe and prefetch hint (owner: Samir) by 2024-11-01.
- Telemetry schema draft for lifecycle events (owner: Observability team) by 2024-11-05.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally rough; looking for feedback on: 1) whether the event set covers most integration needs, 2) the safety model for plugin execution, and 3) the proposed SDK ergonomics (subscribe/once/prefetch). Add comments or inline suggestions; I will reconcile and produce a cleaned PRD for sign-off.

Appendix: short example trace (pseudo) for a tool-backed stream:
- invocation.start -> prefetch.hint(keys: [user_profile]) -> output.delta(x3) -> checkpoint.stable(c1) -> output.delta(x2) -> pretool.invoke(intent: {action: "lookup", entity: "kb:123"}) -> onPretTool hooks run (policy plugin adds auth) -> tool.invoke -> tool.result(streamed frames) -> postprocess.apply -> invocation.finish(summary: {tokens: 412, model: "redwood-13b-quant"})
